examples.japanese: {唐揚|からあ}げを{大皿|おおざら}に{盛|も}った。
examples.english: I served fried chicken on a large plate.

examples.japanese: パーティーでは{大皿|おおざら}に{料理|りょうり}を{出|だ}して、みんなで{取|と}り{分|わ}ける。
examples.english: At parties, we serve food on large platters and everyone helps themselves.

examples.japanese: この{大皿|おおざら}は{祖母|そぼ}から{受|う}け{継|つ}いだものだ。
examples.english: This large platter was handed down from my grandmother.

notes:
{大皿|おおざら} are large plates or platters used for serving food family-style. In Japanese dining, dishes are often placed in the center of the table for everyone to share.

Common uses:
- {大皿|おおざら}{料理|りょうり} (food served family-style)
- {大皿|おおざら}に{盛|も}る (to arrange on a large platter)

Size note: {大皿|おおざら} are typically 25cm or larger in diameter. They are common in {居酒屋|いざかや} and for home entertaining.
